title: Apple’s Foldable iPhone Arrives at $2,000 as Supply Struggles to Meet Demand
author: Daniel Nenni
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Apple’s first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, reached stores worldwide on October 23, pairing a roughly $2,000 price with immediate availability challenges. The debut gives Apple a new premium product while testing whether its customer loyalty can bring folding phones to a wider audience.

Demand quickly exceeded available inventory. Delivery estimates slipped into January shortly after online orders opened, leaving many prospective buyers facing months of waiting. Despite mixed reviews, early adopters rushed to secure a device that offers a substantially different experience from Apple’s familiar smartphone lineup.

Apple limited preorders to two handsets per customer, while several markets restricted launch purchases to customers with existing online orders. Queues nevertheless formed outside stores, and new chief executive John Ternus greeted customers in Austin, Texas. The launch represents an early examination of his leadership following his September appointment.

The hardware has attracted praise for its large interior display, battery life and sturdy construction. However, reviewers also identified drawbacks, including a cramped exterior screen, substantial weight, awkward controls and cameras that struggle to justify the premium price. Those compromises raise questions about its appeal beyond enthusiastic early buyers.

Apple enters a category already served by Samsung and Huawei, making execution especially important. Its opportunity lies in persuading customers that one folding device can handle both everyday phone tasks and activities normally reserved for a tablet. Software adaptation and practical convenience remain central concerns.

Market researcher IDC expects Apple to capture 31% of foldable shipments and 44% of the segment’s value in 2026, potentially leading both measures next year. Those forecasts suggest considerable commercial potential, although sustained success will depend on availability and customer satisfaction. For now, the Duo’s debut combines consumer curiosity with a familiar frustration: finding an available handset.
